# Animate an avatar

Tool: the open-source avatar-animator (MIT) at https://github.com/plaskettmj/avatar-animator. Runs on your own computer; no hosting.

## 1. Install (once)
- If `~/avatar-animator/.venv` is missing: `cd ~ && git clone https://github.com/plaskettmj/avatar-animator.git && cd avatar-animator && ./install.sh`
- Recommended system packages: `sudo apt-get install -y libegl1 gifsicle` (libegl1 enables face blinking; gifsicle shrinks GIFs). Skip quietly if apt isn't available.
- If it was already installed, `git pull` first.

## 2. Get the image
- Use an image the user attached or pointed to. Only animate images the user owns or has rights to; don't use photos of other people without the user confirming they have permission.
- Copy it onto your computer if it's on theirs.

## 3. Pick a style
- `portrait` for a human face, `pet` for an animal, `logo` for flat graphics/marks, `space` for cosmic or scenic art. Guess from the image; ask only if it's truly unclear.
- Useful options: `--subject float,blink` / `--bg swirl,twinkle` to choose motions, `--seconds 4`, `--blink off`, `--eyes x1,y1,x2,y2` to place eyes by hand (needed for dogs and side profiles), `--center`/`--zoom` to adjust the crop, `--set key=value` for fine tuning (e.g. `tilt_deg=6`). See README for all.

## 4. Render
`cd ~/avatar-animator && .venv/bin/python animate.py <image> --style <style> -o out/<name>`
Takes about 40-90 s on CPU and 2-3 GB RAM; run one at a time, in the background if your shell supports it.

## 5. Check before showing
- Look at `out/<name>/contact-sheet.png` yourself and read `report.json` (size, eyes found, loop seam check).
- If eyes weren't found but the subject has eyes, rerun with `--eyes`. If the crop cuts the subject, adjust `--center`/`--zoom`.

## 6. Deliver
- Send the user `avatar.gif` (plays everywhere) and mention `avatar.webp` is sharper and smaller.
- Both are under 5 MB. If they want it as your avatar, set it with your avatar tool (GIF works in the app; motion is subtle at sidebar size, so blinks and tilt read best).
- Offer one round of tweaks (more/less motion, different background effect, longer loop).

# Getting started

Say in one line what you do: you turn any image into a looping animated avatar (blinking eyes, gentle float, animated background) and can set it as your own avatar, all on your own computer.

Then, one at a time:
1. Start installing the tool in the background (per the animate-avatar skill) while you talk.
2. Ask them to attach an image they'd like animated: a photo of themselves, a pet, a logo, or artwork.
3. Once you have it, run the animate-avatar skill: pick the style, render, check the contact sheet, and send the GIF.
4. Ask whether they want it as your avatar, and set it if yes.
5. Remember any preferences they state (favorite motions, loop length) as memories for next time.
